name: Button
definition: A control that runs an action when activated, labelled with the thing it does rather than with where it goes.
useWhen: the control does something instead of going somewhere
notes: The head term that anchors the whole button family. The article should carry the button vs link distinction, which is the most common real question behind the search.

name: Link
definition: A control that navigates somewhere, named for its destination, and carrying the browser affordances of a destination (open in new tab, copy address).
useWhen: the control goes somewhere rather than doing something
notes: Pairs with button as a contrastWith. Accessibility file already holds link-purpose, which is the related but distinct question of what the link text must say.

name: Icon button
definition: A button whose whole label is an icon, so it needs an accessible name and usually a tooltip to say what it does.
useWhen: a square control carrying only a glyph
notes: accessibility.json already holds icon-button-label; keep this record about the control and let that one carry the naming rule.

name: Split button
definition: A two part control where the main area runs a default action and an attached arrow opens a menu of related alternatives.
useWhen: one obvious action plus a menu of its variants
notes: Distinct from menu button: a split button still has a default action you can hit without opening anything.

name: Menu button
definition: A button whose only job is to open a menu, marked with aria-haspopup and usually a downward chevron.
useWhen: the button opens a list of commands, nothing more
notes: Merge candidate with the existing dropdown term. The APG treats the button and the menu as separate patterns, which is the reason to keep both.

name: Toggle button
definition: A button that stays pressed, reporting an on or off state through aria-pressed rather than firing and returning.
useWhen: a button that stays down once you press it
notes: The bold button in a text toolbar is the canonical example. Contrast with switch, which changes a setting immediately and reads as on or off.

name: Toggle group
definition: A set of toggle buttons treated as one control, either single select like radios or multi select like a row of formatting toggles.
useWhen: several toggles that belong to one decision
notes: Merge candidate with the existing segmented-control term. The honest distinction is visual: a segmented control is one continuous track, a toggle group is separate buttons.

name: Button group
definition: Buttons set flush against each other so they read as one unit of related actions, usually with shared borders and rounded outer corners only.
useWhen: several actions that belong together visually

name: Floating action button
definition: A round, raised button that hovers above the content in a fixed corner, carrying the one action the screen is most for.
useWhen: the screen has a single dominant action
notes: Material owns the name. Ant calls the same idea FloatButton, which is worth recording as the naming dispute.

name: Speed dial
definition: A floating action button that fans out into three to six smaller related actions when pressed or hovered.
useWhen: one prominent button that unfolds into a few actions
notes: MUI kept the name after Material 2 dropped it, so the word now lives mostly in React vocabulary.

name: Close button
definition: The small dismiss control in the corner of a dialog, banner or panel, drawn as an X and named Close rather than X.
useWhen: the little X that dismisses a surface
notes: Small enough that most systems ship it as its own component, which is the argument for it being a term.

name: Back to top button
definition: A floating control that appears after you have scrolled a way down and returns the page to the top in one press.
useWhen: a long page needs a shortcut back to the start

name: Ghost button
definition: A button with no fill and often no border until you hover it, sitting at the bottom of the emphasis ladder above a plain link.
useWhen: naming the least emphatic button variant
notes: The variant vocabulary (primary, secondary, tertiary, outline, ghost, destructive) disagrees across systems more than almost any other component naming; this record is the hook for that article.

name: Load more button
definition: A button at the end of a list that appends the next page of results in place instead of navigating to a new page.
useWhen: paging without leaving the current list
notes: The third option between pagination and infinite scroll, and the accessible middle ground. Worth a contrastWith to both.

name: Checkbox
definition: A square control that turns one independent option on or off, used in sets where any number of the options may be chosen.
useWhen: each option is independently on or off
notes: accessibility.json already holds mixed-state-checkbox for the indeterminate third state.

name: Switch
definition: A sliding on or off control that applies its change the moment you flip it, with no separate save step.
useWhen: a setting that takes effect immediately
notes: The checkbox vs switch decision is one of the highest traffic questions in this category; give it a real contrastWith.

name: Slider
definition: A control that sets a value by dragging a handle along a track, showing the whole range at once.
useWhen: picking a value where the range matters more than the number
notes: Its parts are terms of their own: thumb, track, tick marks, value label, stop indicator.

name: Range slider
definition: A slider with two handles on one track that sets a lower and an upper bound, so the selection is an interval rather than a point.
useWhen: the reader picks a from and a to on one track

name: Thumb
definition: The draggable knob on a slider or scrollbar, the part your finger is actually on, as opposed to the track it travels along.
useWhen: naming the draggable part of a slider or scrollbar
notes: Exactly the long tail this site is for. CSS and Windows say thumb, Material says handle, Radix and Ark say Thumb. The MDN row still needs a probe for the pseudo element page.

name: Track
definition: The groove a slider thumb or scrollbar travels along, usually drawn as filled before the handle and empty after it.
useWhen: naming the groove a handle slides in
notes: Old toolkits call it the trough (GTK, Tk), which is a nice piece of history for the article.

name: Tick marks
definition: The small notches printed along a slider track that show the discrete stops the handle can land on.
useWhen: naming the notches printed along a slider
notes: Material 3 renamed these stop indicators in the expressive update, which is worth recording as a live naming change.

name: Stepper
definition: A small two segment control with minus and plus that nudges a number up or down one step at a time.
useWhen: adjusting a number by small known increments
notes: Two hard collisions worth naming in the article: stepper also means the multi step progress bar (see step-indicator), and spinner also means the loading indicator.

name: Step indicator
definition: A row or column of numbered stages showing where you are in a multi step flow and what remains.
useWhen: showing progress through a numbered flow
notes: Direct name collision with stepper the numeric control. Whichever headword canonicalize picks, both must appear as aliases of the other.

name: Text field
definition: A single line box for typed input, carrying a label, an optional hint and the error message when what was typed does not pass.
useWhen: one line of free text or a number

name: Text area
definition: A multi line text box, usually resizable, for input that will not fit or should not be limited to one line.
useWhen: input that runs to several lines
notes: The grow handle in its bottom right corner is the resize-handle term.

name: Search field
definition: A text input specialised for queries, with a magnifier, a clear control and often suggestions that appear as you type.
useWhen: the input is for searching, not for data entry

name: Select
definition: A closed control that shows the current choice and opens a list of options when pressed, with no typing.
useWhen: one choice from a known list, no typing
notes: The select vs combobox vs dropdown three way is the naming question here, and Open UI's customisable select work is the current chapter of it.

name: Listbox
definition: An always visible list of options you choose from with the keyboard or pointer, without a popup or a text field.
useWhen: the options are on screen already, not behind a popup
notes: The role name most people meet only through error messages, which makes it a good dictionary entry.

name: Multi select
definition: A select that accepts several values at once, usually showing the chosen ones as removable tokens inside the field.
useWhen: one field, several answers
notes: Note the interaction file already carries multi-select as the selection gesture (shift click, ctrl click). Merge step must keep these apart or rename one.

name: Token field
definition: An input where each committed entry becomes a small removable pill sitting inside the field, and typing continues after it.
useWhen: free text entries that turn into removable pills
notes: The To field of an email client is the example everyone recognises. Strong tail candidate: many names, no agreed one.

name: PIN input
definition: A row of single character boxes for a short code, where typing advances to the next box and pasting fills them all.
useWhen: entering a short code one character per box
notes: Good demo candidate: the auto advance and the paste behaviour are both scriptable and both are the reason the component exists.

name: Password reveal toggle
definition: The eye control inside a password field that switches the characters between hidden and readable.
useWhen: naming the eye icon inside a password box
notes: No system names the control itself; they all name the field. That gap is exactly what makes it a tail entry.

name: File upload
definition: A control that takes files, by opening the system picker from a button or by accepting a drop into a marked area.
useWhen: the form takes files rather than text
notes: interaction.json already holds drop-zone as the target region; this record is the whole control.

name: Date picker
definition: A field that opens a small calendar so a date can be chosen by looking at the month rather than typing it.
useWhen: choosing a date where the day of week matters
notes: GOV.UK deliberately ships three separate text boxes instead of a calendar, which is a real disagreement worth quoting.

name: Date range picker
definition: A calendar that takes a start and an end date in one pass, highlighting the span between them as you move.
useWhen: the answer is a span of days, not one day

name: Time picker
definition: A control for choosing a time of day, either as a dial you tap around or as hour and minute lists.
useWhen: choosing a clock time

name: Calendar
definition: A month grid of dates that can be read, navigated and selected from, whether standing alone or living inside a date field.
useWhen: a month laid out as a grid of days
notes: Keyboard support is a grid, not a list, which is the interesting half of the entry.

name: Wheel picker
definition: A spinning drum of values that snaps to the item under a fixed selection line, the iOS way of choosing from a short list.
useWhen: the iOS drum you spin to pick a value
notes: Strong tail candidate and a good demo: scroll snap plus a fixed selection band is the whole thing.

name: Rating
definition: A row of stars or similar marks that both shows a score and, when interactive, takes one.
useWhen: a score expressed as filled marks out of five
notes: Half star support and the read only case are the two things every implementation argues about.

name: Transfer list
definition: Two side by side lists with arrow buttons between them, used to move items from available to chosen and back.
useWhen: picking a subset by moving items between two lists
notes: Enterprise vocabulary. Oracle and Salesforce ship it as pick list, PrimeReact as PickList, which is worth a probe later.

name: Cascader
definition: A select whose options open level by level, each choice narrowing the next, used for country then state then city style data.
useWhen: choosing down a hierarchy one level at a time
notes: Miller columns is the older name from the Finder column view and deserves a mention in the article.

name: Tree select
definition: A select whose popup is a tree, so options can be chosen at any depth with parents collapsing over their children.
useWhen: picking from a tree inside a field

name: Floating label
definition: A label that sits inside an empty field and rises to the top edge when the field takes focus or content.
useWhen: the label starts inside the box and moves up
notes: Contested pattern: it solves the placeholder as label problem while creating a smaller one (tiny label, ambiguous empty state). typography.json holds placeholder-as-label already.

name: Helper text
definition: The short line under a field that explains the format or constraint before anything goes wrong.
useWhen: guidance under a field, not an error
notes: Contrast with error message, which appears only after failure and must be tied to the field for screen readers.

name: Error message
definition: The line attached to a field that says what went wrong and what to do about it, announced when it appears.
useWhen: telling one field that its value failed
notes: accessibility.json already holds error-summary and error-identification; this is the per field message.

name: Character counter
definition: The running count beside a text box showing how many characters are used or remain against a limit.
useWhen: showing how much of a length limit is used
notes: The polite live region behaviour (announce at thresholds, not every keystroke) is the reason this deserves an entry.

name: Input mask
definition: A field that imposes a fixed shape as you type, inserting the slashes, spaces or brackets a phone number or card number needs.
useWhen: the field types its own punctuation for you
notes: Widely disliked by accessibility practitioners because it fights paste and assistive input; that argument is the article.

name: Knob
definition: A round control turned by dragging in an arc, borrowed from hardware and mostly found in audio and creative tools.
useWhen: a dial you turn rather than a track you slide

name: Inline edit
definition: Text that reads as plain content until you click it, at which point it becomes an input in the same place with save and cancel.
useWhen: editing a value where it is displayed
notes: The layout shift problem is the interesting constraint: the input must occupy exactly the space the text did.

name: Rich text toolbar
definition: The strip of formatting controls above or beside an editor, whose buttons report their state from wherever the caret sits.
useWhen: the formatting strip over a text editor
notes: Merge candidate with toolbar. Keep separate only if the article is really about pressed state reflecting the selection.

name: Bubble toolbar
definition: A small formatting bar that appears floating over a text selection and disappears when the selection is dropped.
useWhen: the toolbar appears over the text you just selected
notes: Named by editor libraries (Tiptap BubbleMenu, ProseMirror) rather than by design systems, so implementations need a dedicated probe.

name: Code editor
definition: A text area specialised for code, with a gutter of line numbers, syntax colouring and a caret that understands indentation.
useWhen: an editing surface built for code
notes: layout.json already holds gutter in the CSS grid sense; the editor gutter is a different sense of the same word and the merge step should notice.

name: Breadcrumbs
definition: A trail of links showing the path from the top of a hierarchy to the current page, each level clickable on the way back up.
useWhen: showing where a page sits in a hierarchy
notes: What happens when the trail is too long (collapse to an overflow menu in the middle) is the part worth demonstrating.

name: Pagination
definition: The numbered row of page links under a long result set, with previous and next controls and usually an ellipsis where numbers are skipped.
useWhen: results split into numbered pages

name: Navigation bar
definition: The horizontal strip of primary destinations across the top of a site, usually holding the logo, the main sections and an account control.
useWhen: the top strip of site level destinations
notes: Merge candidate with the existing app-bar term, which is the mobile and Material reading of the same strip. NameThatUI treats site header vs navigation bar as a distinction worth drawing.

name: Bottom navigation
definition: A row of three to five destination icons pinned to the bottom of a phone screen, one of them always marked as current.
useWhen: top level destinations within thumb reach
notes: A clean naming collision: Apple says tab bar, Material 3 says navigation bar, and both mean this. Contrast with tabs, which switch panels inside one screen.

name: Mega menu
definition: A large navigation panel that drops from a top level item and shows many links at once, grouped into columns with headings.
useWhen: a nav panel too big to be a simple list

name: Navigation menu
definition: A menu of destinations rather than commands, where opening an item moves you somewhere instead of running an action.
useWhen: a menu whose items are places, not commands
notes: The accessibility point that earns the entry: a nav menu is a list of links in a nav landmark, not a role=menu, and treating it as a menu breaks it.

name: Menu bar
definition: A permanent horizontal row of menu titles (File, Edit, View) whose menus open on click and then follow the pointer along the row.
useWhen: the desktop row of File, Edit, View menus

sources.title: ARIA APG: Menu and Menubar pattern

notes: Its keyboard model (arrow keys move between menus, one tab stop for the whole bar) is the reason it is a pattern rather than a row of buttons.

name: Submenu
definition: A menu that opens sideways from a menu item, marked by a trailing arrow, and stays open while the pointer travels diagonally toward it.
useWhen: a menu that opens out of another menu
notes: The diagonal safe triangle is the detail worth demonstrating and it is already close to interaction.json's hover-intent.

name: Command palette
definition: A keyboard summoned overlay with one search box that finds and runs any command or destination in the application.
useWhen: one keystroke reaches every command by name

sources.title: Command Palette pattern, UX Patterns for Developers

notes: Rich alias set from real products: Blueprint Omnibar, Mantine Spotlight, VS Code Quick Open, Slack quick switcher. The cmdk and Mantine rows still need a page probe.

name: Slash command menu
definition: A menu that opens inside a text field when you type a slash, filtering commands or blocks as you keep typing.
useWhen: typing a slash inside an editor opens the menu

sources.title: Command Palette pattern, UX Patterns for Developers

notes: Popularised by Notion and Slack, and now standard in editors and chat composers. Named by products, not by design systems, so implementation rows need a dedicated probe.

name: Mention
definition: An in-field autocomplete triggered by a marker character such as an at sign, which inserts a reference to a person or object as one unit.
useWhen: typing @ to pull in a person or page

name: Dock
definition: A persistent strip of application icons anchored to a screen edge, holding launchers, running apps and pinned items in one row.
useWhen: the persistent row of app icons at a screen edge
notes: The magnification effect on hover is what most people picture, and it is a good demo. Cross platform naming: dock on macOS, taskbar on Windows, shelf on ChromeOS.

name: Dock badge
definition: The small red count that sits on the corner of an application icon to report unread or pending items.
useWhen: the red count on an app icon
notes: Overlaps the existing badge term. Keep only if the article is really about the OS level count rather than the inline label.

name: Wizard
definition: A flow broken into ordered steps with back and next controls, where each step validates before the next one is allowed.
useWhen: a long task split into ordered steps
notes: Arguably a pattern rather than a component. Recorded here because most systems ship it as a component; the merge step may reassign it.

name: Page indicator
definition: The row of small dots under a carousel or onboarding screen showing how many pages there are and which one you are on.
useWhen: the dots under a swipeable set of screens
notes: Apple's name is page control, which almost nobody outside iOS uses. Good example of a thing everyone can see and few can name.

name: Tree view
definition: A nested list where branches expand and collapse in place, navigated with arrow keys as a single tab stop.
useWhen: nested items that expand in place
notes: AppKit calls it an outline view, which is worth a line in the article.

name: Tree grid
definition: A table whose rows nest and expand like a tree, so hierarchy and columns of data coexist in one grid.
useWhen: a table whose rows contain child rows

name: Toolbar
definition: A grouped row of controls acting on the current view, sharing one tab stop and moving focus between its items with arrow keys.
useWhen: a row of controls acting on what is on screen
notes: accessibility.json already holds roving-tabindex, which is the mechanism this component exists to demonstrate.

name: Ribbon
definition: A tall tabbed toolbar that replaces menus, grouping commands into labelled sections with the important ones drawn larger.
useWhen: the tall tabbed command strip in Office style apps
notes: Microsoft's 2007 answer to menu overload, and still the reference for command dense desktop apps.

name: Scope bar
definition: The row of category buttons directly under a search field that narrows what the query searches, such as All, Mail, Files.
useWhen: buttons under a search box that limit its reach
notes: Apple vocabulary that never crossed to the web, though the thing itself is everywhere in search results pages.

name: Title bar
definition: The strip along the top of a window carrying its title and window controls, and the region you drag to move the window.
useWhen: the draggable strip at the top of a window
notes: Relevant to the web again through the Window Controls Overlay API for installed web apps, which is worth a probe.

name: Window controls
definition: The cluster of close, minimise and zoom controls in a window's title bar, three coloured dots on macOS and three glyphs on Windows.
useWhen: the close, minimise and maximise cluster
notes: Note the platform split in the third button: macOS calls it zoom, Windows calls it maximize, and they do not do the same thing.

name: Menu bar extra
definition: A small application controlled item living in the system menu bar or tray, usually an icon that opens a compact panel of status and controls.
useWhen: an app's icon living in the system bar or tray
notes: Windows calls the region the notification area but everyone says system tray, which is a nice misnomer note.

name: HUD panel
definition: A small dark translucent floating window of controls that hovers over content without taking it over, common in media and creative tools.
useWhen: a small dark floating palette over content

name: Minimap
definition: A shrunken overview of a long document or canvas beside the scrollbar, with a box showing which part is currently on screen.
useWhen: a zoomed out map of a long document or canvas
notes: Named by editors (VS Code, Sublime) and canvas tools (Figma, Miro) rather than by design systems.

name: Scrollbar
definition: The bar beside a scrollable region whose thumb shows both how much content there is and where in it you are.
useWhen: the bar that shows and sets scroll position
notes: color.json already holds scrollbar-color. The overlay vs classic distinction (does it take layout space) is the discrimination worth writing.

name: Splitter
definition: The draggable bar between two panes that changes how much room each one gets, keyboard operable as a slider between limits.
useWhen: the draggable bar between two resizable panes
notes: The APG keyboard model (arrow keys resize, Enter collapses) is the part nobody implements and the reason this entry earns its place.

name: Resize handle
definition: The small corner grip that lets you drag an element or window bigger and smaller, drawn as diagonal ridges on a textarea or window corner.
useWhen: the corner grip that resizes a box
notes: Windows accessibility calls it size grip, which is the most precise name anyone uses. The MDN row needs a probe for the resize property page.

name: Divider
definition: A thin line separating groups of content, decorative when the grouping is already clear and semantic when it is the only cue.
useWhen: a line that groups content by separating it
notes: Divider vs separator vs rule is a genuine three way naming split, and the accessibility difference (decorative vs role=separator) is real.

name: Disclosure
definition: A single button that shows and hides one region of content, reporting its state through aria-expanded.
useWhen: one control hiding one region
notes: Overlaps the existing accordion term. The distinction that holds: an accordion is a set of disclosures that know about each other.

name: Disclosure triangle
definition: The small triangle beside a tree item that points right when collapsed and down when open, rotating as it toggles.
useWhen: the little triangle that opens a branch
notes: Exemplary tail term: everyone has clicked one, almost nobody can name it, and Windows draws it as plus and minus instead.

name: Chevron
definition: The small angle bracket used as a directional marker: down means this opens, right means this goes deeper, in breadcrumbs it means next level.
useWhen: naming the little angle arrow on a control
notes: Collides with typography's caret (the text insertion point) and with the CSS caret-color property, which typography.json already covers.

name: Data table
definition: A table built for working with data rather than reading it: sortable headers, selectable rows, sticky headers and per row actions.
useWhen: rows of data you sort, select and act on
notes: Its parts are their own tail terms: sort indicator, column resizer, row selection checkbox, frozen column, zebra striping.

name: Data grid
definition: A spreadsheet-like table where individual cells take focus and can be edited, navigated cell by cell with the arrow keys.
useWhen: a table you move around cell by cell

implementations.name: Grid (Interactive Tabular Data and Layout Containers)

notes: Data table vs data grid is a real discrimination (row focus vs cell focus) that almost every product blurs. TanStack row needs a probe.

name: Sort indicator
definition: The small arrow in a column header showing that the table is sorted by that column and in which direction.
useWhen: the arrow in a header showing the sort
notes: The aria-sort attribute is what makes it real to a screen reader, which ties this to accessibility.json.

name: Column resizer
definition: The invisible strip on a column border that widens or narrows the column when dragged, and often fits the column to its content on double click.
useWhen: dragging a column border to change its width
notes: A good demo for hit slop: the visible line is one pixel and the target is eight.

name: Expandable row
definition: A table row that opens to reveal a detail panel beneath it, keeping the row in place instead of navigating away.
useWhen: row detail that opens in place under the row

name: Zebra striping
definition: Alternating row backgrounds in a table so the eye can track a single row across many columns.
useWhen: shading every other row of a table
notes: Could reasonably be filed under aesthetic or accessibility rather than component; recorded here because it only exists inside tables.

name: Virtual scrolling
definition: Rendering only the rows currently in view and faking the rest with spacer height, so a list of a million items scrolls at speed.
useWhen: a list too long to render all at once
notes: A technique more than a component, but it is what people search for when their find in page stops working. May belong in pattern.

name: Card
definition: A bounded surface holding a preview of one thing, usually an image, a title, some detail and one or two actions, that as a whole leads somewhere.
useWhen: one thing previewed on its own surface
notes: The whole card clickable problem (nested links, text selection, right click) is the hard part and the reason for the article.

name: Selection card
definition: A radio or checkbox dressed as a card, where the whole tile is the target and the control itself is small or absent.
useWhen: choosing between options drawn as big tiles

name: Description list
definition: Paired labels and values laid out as a list of facts about one thing, rather than as a table of many things.
useWhen: labelled facts about a single record
notes: Six systems, six names, one thing: a strong candidate for the naming table this site is for.

name: Avatar
definition: A small image standing in for a person or entity, falling back to initials or a generic glyph when there is no picture.
useWhen: a person represented by a small image
notes: Fluent's Persona is the notable alternative name and it means avatar plus name plus secondary line.

name: Avatar group
definition: Several avatars overlapped in a row to show a set of people compactly, with a plus n counter standing for the rest.
useWhen: a row of overlapping faces with a plus n
notes: Facepile is the older Facebook name and still widely spoken, worth recording as an alias with that provenance.

name: Presence indicator
definition: The small coloured dot on an avatar reporting whether a person is available, away, busy or offline.
useWhen: the green dot on someone's picture
notes: Colour alone carries the meaning here, which puts it straight into the use-of-color accessibility discussion.

name: Timeline
definition: A vertical or horizontal line of dated events, each pinned to the line by a marker and reading in order.
useWhen: events in order along a line
notes: Collides with the media editing sense of timeline (the track editor), which is worth disambiguating in the article.

name: Stat
definition: A single number shown large with a label and often a change indicator, the unit a dashboard is built from.
useWhen: one number shown big with its label

name: Sparkline
definition: A tiny chart with no axes or labels, drawn inline at text size to show the shape of a trend beside the number it belongs to.
useWhen: a trend line small enough to sit inline
notes: Coined by Edward Tufte, which gives the article a genuine provenance to cite.

name: Progress bar
definition: A filling bar reporting how far along a task is, determinate when the end is known and indeterminate when it is not.
useWhen: showing how far through a task you are
notes: Progress vs meter is the discrimination worth writing: progress moves toward completion, a meter reports a level.

name: Progress ring
definition: A circular progress indicator that fills around a ring, often with the percentage in the middle.
useWhen: progress drawn as a filling circle
notes: Frequently confused with the spinner, which reports that something is happening rather than how much is done.

name: Meter
definition: A gauge of a known quantity within a known range, such as disk used or password strength, where the level is a fact rather than a task.
useWhen: a level within a known range, not a task
notes: AppKit's level indicator has four styles (relevancy, capacity, rating, continuous) and is the richest naming source for this idea.

name: Gauge
definition: A dial style readout showing one value on an arc between a minimum and a maximum, borrowed from instrument panels.
useWhen: a value read off an arc like a dial
notes: SwiftUI ships Gauge as a first class control, which is the strongest claim on the name.

name: Tag
definition: A small label attached to an item to classify it, often coloured by category and sometimes removable.
useWhen: a small label that classifies an item
notes: Merge candidate with the existing chip and badge terms. NameThatUI treats badge vs chip vs pill vs tag as one entry, which is a reasonable alternative shape.

name: Keyboard key
definition: A key drawn as a small keycap in running text or a menu, so a shortcut reads as something you press rather than something you say.
useWhen: printing a key the reader should press
notes: interaction.json already holds keyboard-shortcut and modifier-key; this is the visual component that prints them.

name: QR code
definition: A square matrix barcode rendered in the interface to hand a link or credential to a phone camera.
useWhen: handing a link to a phone by camera

name: Thumbnail
definition: A small stand-in image for a larger one, cropped rather than letterboxed so a row of them lines up.
useWhen: a small preview image of a bigger one
notes: Collides with thumb the slider handle, which is worth one line of disambiguation.

name: Carousel
definition: A row of items shown a few at a time that advances by arrows, swipe or a timer, with the rest waiting off screen.
useWhen: a set of items shown a few at a time in a row
notes: Watch the alias trap: carousel is often called a slider, which is a different component entirely. Embla row needs a probe.

name: Filmstrip
definition: A scrollable row of thumbnails beside a larger view, where picking one changes what the large view shows.
useWhen: a thumbnail rail that drives a big preview

name: Lightbox
definition: An overlay that shows one image or video large over a dimmed page, with next and previous controls and a dismiss.
useWhen: an image opened large over the dimmed page
notes: The name comes from a 2005 JavaScript library and stuck; almost no design system uses it, which is itself the story.

name: Callout
definition: A boxed note set into the flow of content to carry a warning, tip or aside, coloured by severity and staying put once shown.
useWhen: a boxed note sitting inside the content
notes: The alert, banner, callout, toast family is the messiest naming cluster in this category. banner and toast already exist on the site, so this record must be scoped to the in-flow box.

name: Toggletip
definition: A tip revealed by clicking rather than hovering, so it works by touch and may contain links or controls a tooltip could not.
useWhen: a hint you click open, not hover open
notes: Heydon Pickering coined the split. The distinction is genuinely load bearing for accessibility and makes a clean contrastWith against the existing tooltip term.

name: Popover arrow
definition: The small triangle joining a popover or tooltip to the thing it belongs to, which flips and slides as the popover repositions.
useWhen: the little triangle pointing at the trigger
notes: Everyone ships one, everyone calls it Arrow in code, and nobody documents the word. Perfect long tail entry; Floating UI's arrow middleware is the reference behaviour.

name: Coach mark
definition: A temporary message anchored to a control that teaches what it does, often chained into a numbered sequence across a screen.
useWhen: a teaching bubble pointing at a control
notes: The multi step tour built from these is arguably a pattern; this record is the single bubble.

name: Popconfirm
definition: A small confirmation bubble anchored to the control you just pressed, asking are you sure without opening a dialog.
useWhen: confirming in place instead of in a dialog
notes: Ant coined the portmanteau and it has spread widely in Chinese and enterprise React work without ever entering Western design system vocabulary.

name: Confirmation dialog
definition: A modal that stops an action to ask whether you meant it, naming the consequence in the button rather than saying OK.
useWhen: stopping a destructive action to ask

sources.title: ARIA APG: Alert and Message Dialogs pattern

notes: Merge candidate with the existing alert-dialog term. The interesting argument is undo instead of confirm, which links to the existing undo entry.

name: Action sheet
definition: A modal list of choices that slides up from the bottom of a phone screen in response to something you just did, with cancel at the end.
useWhen: choices for an action you just started, on a phone

sources.title: Action sheets, Apple Human Interface Guidelines

notes: Contrast with bottom sheet: an action sheet is a short list of commands, a bottom sheet is a surface that can hold anything.

name: Bottom sheet
definition: A surface anchored to the bottom edge that slides up over the content, often draggable between a peeked and an expanded height.
useWhen: a panel that rises from the bottom edge
notes: The site already has drawer, so this record must argue the edge and the drag, not just the overlay. Vaul row needs a probe.

name: Grabber
definition: The short rounded bar drawn at the top of a bottom sheet to say the surface can be dragged.
useWhen: the little bar on top of a sheet
notes: interaction.json already holds drag-handle for the reorder grip. Apple says grabber and Material says drag handle for this specific bar, which is why it is worth splitting.

name: Tearsheet
definition: A tall modal anchored to the bottom of the viewport that holds a multi step creation flow, stackable when one flow opens another.
useWhen: a full height modal for a creation flow
notes: IBM-only vocabulary borrowed from print advertising. Worth recording precisely because it is the kind of word people meet once and cannot place.

name: Share sheet
definition: The system panel of destinations and actions for sending the current item elsewhere, populated by whatever apps are installed.
useWhen: the system panel for sending something onward
notes: Apple's formal name is activity view, which nobody says. The Web Share API brings the same sheet to the browser and deserves an implementation row after a probe.

name: Notification center
definition: A panel collecting notifications that were missed or kept, usually opened from a bell with an unread count.
useWhen: the panel behind the bell icon
notes: The counterpart to toast: toasts are the ones you may miss, this is where they go.

name: Chat bubble
definition: A rounded container for one message in a conversation, aligned and coloured by who sent it, often with a tail toward the sender's side.
useWhen: one message in a conversation view
notes: Newly standard vocabulary: several systems added chat components in 2024 and 2025 for assistant interfaces.

name: Typing indicator
definition: The three bouncing dots shown while someone is composing a reply, or while an assistant is preparing one.
useWhen: showing that a reply is being composed
notes: MUI draws a useful distinction: a typing indicator means a human is composing, a streaming indicator means a model is generating.

name: Prompt input
definition: The composer at the bottom of an assistant interface: a growing text area with attachment, model and send controls attached to it.
useWhen: the box you type an assistant request into
notes: Auto growing height without shifting the messages above it is the layout constraint that makes it a good specimen.

name: Emoji picker
definition: A searchable grid of emoji organised by category, with recent choices remembered and skin tone chosen once.
useWhen: choosing an emoji from a searchable grid

name: Reaction picker
definition: A small row of emoji that appears on hover or long press so a message can be answered without a reply.
useWhen: answering a message with one emoji

name: Property filter
definition: A search field that builds structured queries from tokens, letting a reader filter by named properties with operators rather than free text.
useWhen: filtering by named fields inside one search box
notes: GitHub's issue search and Linear's filter bar are the two examples everyone recognises.

name: Faceted filter
definition: A panel of grouped checkboxes and ranges that narrows a result set, each option usually showing how many results it would leave.
useWhen: narrowing results by category with counts
notes: The count beside each option is the part that makes it faceted rather than just a list of checkboxes.

name: Bulk action bar
definition: A bar that appears once rows are selected, replacing the normal controls with actions that apply to the selection and a count of it.
useWhen: actions that appear once you select rows
notes: Good no-layout-shift demo: the bar has to appear without pushing the table down.

name: Attribute editor
definition: A repeating row of key and value fields with add and remove controls, used for tags, headers and other open ended pairs.
useWhen: a form section that repeats a row of fields
notes: Focus management after removing a row is the accessibility detail worth demonstrating.

name: Task list
definition: A list of the steps in a longer application, each with a status tag, so a reader can leave and come back knowing what remains.
useWhen: a checklist of steps across several sittings
notes: GOV.UK's task list pattern is the reference; SaaS onboarding checklists are the same component with different stakes.

name: Show more toggle
definition: The control at the end of clamped text that expands it to full length and, when honest, collapses it again.
useWhen: expanding text that was cut off after n lines
notes: typography.json already holds line-clamp and truncation; this is the control that undoes them.

name: Color well
definition: The small filled square that shows the current colour and opens a colour picker when pressed.
useWhen: the little colour square that opens a picker
notes: AppKit's NSColorWell is where the name comes from. color.json already holds color-picker and swatch, so this record is only the trigger.

name: Combo button
definition: A macOS control that acts as a button but carries a small arrow opening a menu of alternatives, Apple's reading of the split button.
useWhen: the Apple name for a button with a menu arrow
notes: Merge candidate with split-button. Apple's pop-up vs pull-down button distinction (does it show the current value or a fixed title) is the genuinely useful part.

name: Scrubber
definition: The seek control of a media player: a track showing elapsed and buffered time with a playhead you drag to move through it.
useWhen: the bar you drag to move through a video
notes: interaction.json already holds scrubbing as the gesture; this is the control it acts on.

name: Playhead
definition: The marker showing the current position in a timeline or track, which travels during playback and can be dragged to move it.
useWhen: the marker showing where playback is
notes: Video editing vocabulary that most web people never learn even though they use it daily.

name: Media controls
definition: The cluster of play, pause, skip, volume and fullscreen controls attached to a player, which usually hides itself while playing.
useWhen: the control bar of a video or audio player

name: Waveform
definition: An audio track drawn as a row of amplitude bars, used both to show what is in the file and as the surface you scrub along.
useWhen: audio drawn as bars you can scrub

name: Watermark
definition: Repeating faint text or a mark tiled across content to claim it or to mark it as a draft or a preview.
useWhen: faint repeated text laid over content

name: Signature pad
definition: A drawing area that captures a handwritten signature by pointer or touch, with a clear control and a baseline to sign on.
useWhen: capturing a handwritten signature
notes: Needs a keyboard alternative to be usable at all, which is the interesting half of the entry.

name: CAPTCHA
definition: A challenge placed in a form to sort people from scripts, from distorted text to a single checkbox that watches how you got there.
useWhen: the challenge that proves you are a person
notes: accessibility.json already holds accessible-authentication, which is where the WCAG argument against CAPTCHAs lives. Keep the two linked.

name: Cookie banner
definition: The consent notice shown on a first visit, offering accept, reject and settings before any optional cookie is set.
useWhen: the consent notice on a first visit
notes: Arguably a pattern rather than a component, but GOV.UK ships it as a component and it is what people search for.

name: Fieldset
definition: A group of related form controls sharing one question, with a legend that acts as the label for the whole group.
useWhen: several controls answering one question
notes: The legend is the part that matters and the part everyone omits, which is the article.

name: Action list
definition: A vertical list of commands with icons, descriptions and dividers, the shared body used inside menus, panels and side sheets.
useWhen: a list of commands reused inside several surfaces
notes: Primer's split of ActionList (the body) from ActionMenu (the trigger and popover) is the clearest statement of why this is its own component.

name: Utility bar
definition: A persistent bar docked to the bottom of an application holding small tools that open into panels without leaving the current page.
useWhen: tools docked along the bottom of the app
notes: Salesforce vocabulary. The chat windows docked along the bottom of Gmail and Facebook are the same idea under no name at all.

name: Welcome mat
definition: A full width introduction shown on first entry to a feature, listing what is new or what to set up, with a way to skip it for good.
useWhen: a first run introduction to a whole feature
notes: Salesforce named it and Open UI's matrix picked the name up, which is the only reason it has any currency outside Salesforce.

name: Image comparison slider
definition: Two images stacked with a draggable divider that wipes between them, used to show a before and an after in one frame.
useWhen: showing before and after in one frame
notes: Almost no design system ships it and almost every product marketing page has one, which is exactly the gap this site fills.

name: Copy button
definition: A small control beside a value that copies it to the clipboard and confirms by turning into a tick for a second or two.
useWhen: copying a value with one press
notes: The confirmation has to be announced, not only drawn, which is the accessibility half of the entry.

name: Relative timestamp
definition: A time printed as a distance from now, two hours ago or in three days, updating itself and holding the exact time in its tooltip.
useWhen: printing a time as how long ago it was
notes: Intl.RelativeTimeFormat is the platform answer and deserves an MDN row after a probe. The Mantine row is a weak match and should probably be dropped.

name: Comparison table
definition: A table whose columns are options and whose rows are features, read across to decide between plans or products.
useWhen: deciding between options feature by feature
notes: The hard part is the mobile reading, where the columns have to become cards or the header has to stick sideways.

name: Model selector
definition: The control in an assistant interface that picks which model answers, usually a menu carrying a short description of each option.
useWhen: choosing which model answers the request
notes: New vocabulary, still settling. Worth an entry precisely because the naming is being decided now.

name: Keyboard shortcuts dialog
definition: The panel opened by pressing question mark that lists every shortcut in the application, grouped by area.
useWhen: the cheat sheet of every shortcut
notes: Gmail, GitHub, Linear and Slack all ship one behind the same question mark key, which is a strong convention with no agreed name.

name: Emergency exit button
definition: A control that leaves the current page immediately for an unrelated site and tries to clear it from history, for readers who may be watched.
useWhen: leaving a page fast and without a trace
notes: Triggered by pressing Shift three times as well as by the button. Rare, specific and genuinely important, which is the best kind of tail entry.

name: Form
definition: A grouping of controls a reader fills in and submits together, carrying the labels, validation and submit affordance for the whole set.
useWhen: a set of inputs is submitted as one unit
notes: Head term above the whole input family. Has to earn its keep against the more specific field terms, so lean on submit semantics, grouping and the validation contract rather than on styling.

name: Icon
definition: A small graphic symbol standing for an action, object or idea, read at a glance and rarely safe to ship without a label.
useWhen: a symbol has to carry meaning in very little space
notes: The most implemented entry in The Component Gallery (45 examples) and still missing from round one. Distinct from icon-button, which is the control, and icon-font, which is the delivery mechanism.

name: Image
definition: An embedded picture, sized and cropped by the layout around it, carrying the alternative text that stands in when it cannot be seen.
useWhen: a picture is content rather than decoration

name: List
definition: A vertical run of related items presented as a set, where the shared shape of every row is what tells a reader the rows belong together.
useWhen: items are peers and the set matters more than any one row
notes: The umbrella above description-list, action-list and task-list. Worth keeping because the three HTML list types (unordered, ordered, description) are a real and frequently muddled distinction.

name: Rich text editor
definition: An editing surface that shows formatting as it will appear rather than as markup, so what the writer sees is close to what readers get.
useWhen: authors need formatting without learning a markup language

sources.title: The Component Gallery: Rich text editor

notes: The editor itself, as opposed to rich-text-toolbar (the controls) and bubble-toolbar (the selection popover), both of which already exist and should relate up to this one.

name: Video player
definition: A framed video with the controls needed to play, seek, mute and caption it, sized so the controls never crowd the picture.
useWhen: video is the content and the reader controls playback
notes: media-controls already covers the control bar in isolation; this is the framed player around it, which is where poster frames, aspect ratio and caption placement live.

name: File attachment
definition: A row or card standing in for a file, showing its type, name and size, with the one action that file supports: download, open or remove.
useWhen: a file has to be represented rather than uploaded
notes: Deliberately split from file-upload: that term is the drop target, this one is the representation of a file that already exists.

name: Input group
definition: A field welded to text, a button or a select at one or both ends, so the addon reads as part of the same control rather than as a neighbour.
useWhen: a unit, prefix or action belongs inside the field
notes: The interesting part for an article is the seam: focus ring, border collapse and hit area all have to treat the group as a single control.

name: Figure
definition: An image, table or code block bound to its caption so the two travel together and can be referred to from the running text.
useWhen: a visual needs a caption that belongs to it

name: Tag input
definition: A field that turns each entry into a removable tag sitting inside the field, with the caret waiting after the last one.
useWhen: a reader types an open ended set of short values
notes: Blueprint composes this with a dropdown to make MultiSelect, which is the right way round: the tag field is the primitive. Backspace deleting the last tag is the behaviour readers come looking for.

name: Lockup
definition: A fixed grouping of a content view with its header and footer that grows, shrinks and takes focus as a single unit.
useWhen: several views must behave as one focusable object
notes: tvOS vocabulary, and the clearest name anywhere for the thing the web keeps calling a card. HIG defines four kinds: cards, caption buttons, monograms and posters. The shared focus growth is the point.

name: Ornament
definition: A small panel of controls that floats just outside a window edge in visionOS, staying with the window without covering its contents.
useWhen: controls must stay reachable without eating the content

sources.title: Create with Swift: Creating Ornaments in visionOS

notes: Spatial vocabulary with no web equivalent, which is exactly what makes it worth defining. On visionOS tab bars and toolbars become ornaments by default.

name: Image well
definition: An editable image view that shows its current picture and accepts a replacement dragged or pasted straight into it.
useWhen: a picture is both the display and the drop target
notes: The macOS name for the profile picture control every web app builds and never names. Copy, paste and delete are expected to work on it.

name: Virtual keyboard
definition: The on screen keyboard a device raises for a field, whose key set the field itself chooses by declaring what kind of value it wants.
useWhen: the field type decides which keys a reader is given
notes: The design decision is upstream in the field: an email keyboard with an @ key, a numeric pad for a code. Also the thing that eats half the viewport and moves the submit button.

name: Complication
definition: A slot on a watch face filled with one live figure from an app, sized to be read in the second a wrist is raised.
useWhen: one number has to survive being glanced at on a watch
notes: Borrowed from watchmaking, where a complication is any function beyond telling the time. watchOS 9 organises them into families (circular, inline and others) with recommended layouts.

name: Live activity
definition: A persistent, updating view of something in progress, shown in system places like a lock screen so a reader can follow it without opening the app.
useWhen: a task in progress must be followed outside the app
notes: Defined against the push notification: not one interruption but a few hours of state, and interactive. The food delivery tracker is the canonical example.

name: Widget
definition: A small, glanceable view of an app placed on a system surface such as a home screen or desktop, sized in fixed slots rather than freely.
useWhen: app content is useful without opening the app
notes: Worth disambiguating in the article: ARIA also calls any composite control a widget, which is a different word wearing the same spelling.

name: Quick settings tile
definition: A one tap button or toggle an app contributes to the system control surface, so one feature can be reached without opening the app.
useWhen: one app feature deserves a place in system controls

sources.title: Android: Create custom Quick Settings tiles

notes: Named after the Android term on purpose: Apple calls these Controls, which collides head on with the generic sense of control. Symbol, title and optional value is the whole anatomy.

name: App shortcut
definition: A short menu of app actions hung off the app icon itself, opened by a long press or a secondary click before the app is even running.
useWhen: a frequent action should skip the app launch

sources.title: Apple HIG: Home Screen quick actions

notes: HIG itself ties Dock menus and Home Screen quick actions together as one idea, so they are merged here. Not to be confused with the separate HIG App Shortcuts page, which is about App Intents and Siri.

name: Push notification
definition: A system delivered message shown outside the app, on a lock screen or in a notification list, that has to earn the interruption it costs.
useWhen: something needs saying while the app is closed
notes: Distinct from toast, which lives inside the app and cannot interrupt anything. The consent prompt in front of it is why permission-priming exists.

name: Chart
definition: A drawing of data in which position, length, angle or colour carries the numbers, chosen so the comparison a reader needs is the easiest one to see.
useWhen: numbers are easier compared by eye than by reading
notes: Round one caught sparkline and gauge but not the head term above them. The article should carry the encoding choice (position beats angle beats area) rather than a chart type list.
